transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Well, thank you for seeing me. I... I'm here because I just seem to worry about absolutely everything now. My clients, the state of the market, my family, money, even whether moving to the new condo was the right decision. We just downsized, and honestly, trying to fit my old dining set into that new open-concept layout was a complete nightmare. I ended up having to sell my beautiful mahogany table on Facebook Marketplace, and the woman who bought it showed up two hours late in a sedan. I mean, who tries to fit a heavy six-seater table into a Honda Accord? I had to stand there in the driveway in the heat helping her tie the trunk down with bungee cords, and she didn't even bring moving blankets. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. The worrying. It just feels completely out of proportion to what is actually happening in my life, and I just can't seem to stop stressing over every little thing.
How often do you feel anxious or worried throughout the day, and does it seem to happen regardless of what you're doing or where you are?

Oh, it's pretty much all day. It really doesn't matter where I am or what I'm doing. Like, just on Tuesday, I was showing a property over in the Heights—beautiful split-level, great bones, but the staging was just atrocious. They had this modern, bright blue velvet sofa right next to a distressed farmhouse coffee table. It clashed so terribly, I honestly don't know what the listing agent was thinking. And they were burning some sort of overly sweet vanilla candle that just clung to the air. I kept thinking about how buyers hate strong smells, it makes them think you're hiding water damage or pet odors. 

But anyway, I'm standing there, supposed to be pointing out the upgraded windows to my clients, and my mind is just spinning about my own life. Even when I tell myself, 'Parin, this is not urgent,' one concern just leads right into another. And before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour just standing there replaying small details I meant to let go of, completely ignoring the house. So yes, it just happens everywhere.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like restlessness, fatigue, trouble concentrating, muscle tension, or sleep disturbances along with your worrying?

Well, you know, it's funny you mention trouble concentrating, because that's really been bothering me lately. Like, when I'm reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums, I'll read the same paragraph three or four times because a worry pops in and I just completely lose the thread of what I was checking. And those addendums, I tell you, they are getting longer and longer every year. It used to be a simple one-page form, maybe two if the roof was old, but now? Now everybody wants a special clause for everything. I had one buyer last month who insisted on writing in a contingency about the neighbor's oak tree dropping leaves in the pool. I tried to tell him, 'Sir, you're buying a house in a neighborhood with mature trees, you're going to get some leaves,' but he wouldn't listen. We went back and forth with the seller's agent for three days over a tree. A tree! And the seller's agent, she was new, clearly had no idea what she was doing. She kept sending the documents over as blurry JPEGs instead of PDFs. I had to call her broker to get it sorted out. 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. The concentration. Yes, I just can't seem to focus on the paperwork anymore without my mind wandering off to some other problem.
Have you been having trouble with muscle tension or sleep lately, like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Well, sleep has definitely been an issue. Most nights I get into bed at a reasonable hour, you know, around 10:30, maybe 11:00 if I've been watching that new home renovation show on HGTV. Although, I have to say, the designs on that show are just entirely unrealistic for most buyers' budgets. They act like everyone has an extra hundred thousand dollars lying around to knock down load-bearing walls and install custom Italian marble countertops. And the contractors! They always seem to find some "unexpected" plumbing issue that adds two weeks to the timeline. In the real world, my clients would be having an absolute meltdown if a contractor tried to pull that on them right before closing. Just last year, I had a seller who decided to DIY their bathroom remodel to save a few bucks, and they used the wrong kind of grout. The entire shower started leaking into the kitchen downstairs three days before the final walkthrough. We had to scramble to get a professional in there, and the buyers almost walked away. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, right, sleep. Yes, so I get into bed, but my mind just keeps circling through everything. Condo fees, tomorrow’s showings, whether I missed some tiny detail in a contract. It takes me forever to finally settle down, and even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I never really rested at all.
Do you often feel physically restless or tense, like you can't relax even when you want to?

Well, yes, actually. I do feel tense. By the time evening rolls around, my neck and shoulders are just... they feel so tight, like I've been bracing myself all day. And I've started catching myself clenching my jaw, especially when I'm driving between listings. Traffic on the I-10 has been just a nightmare lately. They've had that construction going near the Washington exit for what feels like three years now. They put up those orange barrels, close two lanes, and then you never see a single worker actually out there doing anything! It took me forty-five minutes just to get across town on Thursday to show a lovely little bungalow. And of course, the client was late anyway. They always say they're "five minutes away" when they haven't even left their house. It's so disrespectful of my time, honestly. 

And then when I'm sitting at my desk, trying to catch up on emails, I'll realize my jaw is just locked tight again. I had to go to the dentist last month because I thought I cracked a tooth, but he said it was just from grinding. He tried to sell me this custom night guard for six hundred dollars! Can you believe that? Six hundred dollars for a little piece of plastic. I told him I could buy a whole new dishwasher for one of my rental properties for that price. 

But, um, yes. The tension. It's definitely there, in my shoulders and my jaw, even when I'm just trying to sit and get work done.
